title: Isolation and freezing of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells from pregnant patients
protocol: Invert Ficoll-Paque PLUS several times.
Place 17 mL Ficoll-Paque PLUS medium into the SepMate™-50 tube by carefully pipetting it through the central hole of the SepMate™-50 insert (Ficoll to be just above the insert).
Transfer blood to a separate 50 mL Falcon tube in a sterile manner.
Dilute the blood 1:1 in PBS-EDTA with 2% FBS, close the tube and mix by careful inversion.
Add diluted sample to SepMate™-50 tube by pipetting it down the side of the tube.
Centrifuge at 1200×g for 20 min at room temperature, with the brake on.
Remove some of the plasma layer without disturbing the interface with the PBMCs.
Pour off the top layer containing enriched MNCs into a new 50 mL Falcon tube.
Do not hold the SepMate™ tube inverted for more than 2 seconds to avoid disrupting the filter.
Register cryovials using the barcode and record them as PBMCs.
Fill the 50 mL falcon tube with RPMI 1640 medium and mix carefully.
Centrifuge at 300×g at 20°C for 8 minutes and discard the supernatant.
Repeat steps using 5–10 mL PBS-EDTA with 2% FBS.
Centrifuge again for 8 minutes at 300×g at 20°C.
Pour off excess PBS-EDTA with 2% FBS without disturbing the pellet.
Count and resuspend cells in 1 mL of freezing medium DMSO.
Ensure cryovials are resting on ice or in an icebox.
Aliquot cells into one barcoded cryovial, holding it on wet ice until freezing begins within 5 minutes.
Freeze cells in the Corning CoolCell chamber below –70°C.
Transfer the cells to cryo boxes after at least 12 h.
Record the position of the cells in the cryo boxes.
Place the cryo boxes in a −80°C freezer for 12–24 hours (maximum four days).
Transfer the cryovials from the −80°C freezer into the liquid nitrogen tank.
